title: perf(update): prototype clone-first runtime retention
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Native updates currently hash every installed dependency file before retaining the running updater. This draft tests whether independent filesystem clones can remove that full hash pass without weakening retention integrity.

## User Impact

This is an unqualified owner prototype and must not be merged. A successful clone becomes the retained byte authority; unsupported capture or source mutation drains and discards that attempt before selecting the existing complete hash/link backend once. No dependency or schema change. The existing update lifecycle and native-helper cleanup owners remain responsible.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shipped fs-safe 0.26.13 public `Root.copyIn` descriptor source and `clone: "always"` provide independent bytes before inventory and control-file parsing. The shared graph owner accepts a capture policy while its original hashing policy remains the fallback. Windows and cross-device capture use the existing backend. Source ctime-only hard-link churn must retain existing availability through fallback.

## Evidence

Preregistered Stage 1 acceptance, before any owner or timed sample:

- Flow: the real runtime-retention subprocess and owner transport, synthetic installed tree, 312 packages × 512 one-KiB payloads plus manifests/entrypoints: 160,370 regular files and 161,309 entries. Both arms use identical Node 26.12.1, fixture bytes, volume, concurrency, workload and dependencies. Baseline is `2937d6581241ca1854601c3ab7a8594838352a49`; exact candidate source hashes are retained with the experiment.
- Counts first: filesystem operations/bytes, worker requests, successful independent clones, hash work, returned file counts, SQL and MAIN. Native internal syscalls are not inferred from JS counts. Capture CPU profiles separately from timing.
- Warm timing: excluded A/B warmup, then at least five alternating A/B pairs, fresh helper/private destination each time, reused source. Use the campaign timing lock, proof slot, load1 <24 before each sample, and at least 10 GiB internal free. Report median, nearest-rank p95, min–max and every sample. Cold filesystem is unmeasured unless a clean method becomes immediately available; new-process runs are not cold-filesystem evidence.
- PASS requires at least 25% lower retention-wall median. Retention wall, helper wall, helper-plus-cleanup wall, total process CPU, main-thread CPU, RSS and success/file counts must hold or improve. Any 20% adverse median or p95 cell stops qualification. A worker move is not a saving. Record resource/disk allocation costs separately.
- If no qualified timing can start within 60 minutes of lock/load waiting, report counts/profiles only and mark the wall-time floor UNPROVEN. No PASS without qualified samples. An isolated remote replacement is permitted only if granted immediately; both arms must use that platform.
- Stage 1 stops after PASS, FLOOR, or UNMEASURED. Production functional qualification, two final isolated reviews, matched native X versus X+patch proof, exact-head CI, overlap checks and landing are later gates.

Current status: **FLOOR — closed as not planned by coordinator disposition after owner counts.** The count regression crosses the adverse-cell stop rule. The controller was canceled while waiting for the shared timing lock; zero warmups or qualified timing samples ran. Warm and cold wall time remain unmeasured, so this is not a measured wall-time floor. The >=25% retention-wall improvement is unproven. No production qualification or landing is claimed.

The frozen dependency install completed on 2026-10-30 with pinned pnpm 12.15.0; formatting and whitespace checks passed. Two isolated Codex source reviews found no P0–P2 findings, with execution and traversal-context limitations explicitly retained. The owner count pair and separate per-thread profiles completed. No real installation or operator state was used.

Static-check limitation: the lint wrapper stopped before linting because its declaration-boundary preparation rejects dependencies physically outside the checkout. This experiment uses the required separate dependency store; no wrapper bypass or dependency relocation was used.

### Stage 1 counts (160,370 files; 161,309 entries)

| Metric per retention | Baseline | Clone prototype |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Source hard links | 160,057 | 0 |
| Independent copies/clones | 313 | 160,370 |
| Hash worker requests | 159,347 | 0 |
| Initial hash bytes | 163,603,928 | 0 |
| Visible filesystem API calls, all non-observer domains | 3,730,713 | 11,876,278 |
| SQL statements / runtime MAIN | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |

The filesystem-call increase is 218.3%, dominated by repeated metadata/admission/publication work. This is a real work-count regression, not a thread move hidden by the request reduction. Counts cover observed JavaScript APIs, including startup and ancestor-path work, not unobserved native syscalls or FileHandle methods.

Instrumentation-bearing diagnostics (not the timing gate): total helper CPU 733.564 -> 1,443.090 seconds; main-thread CPU 148.507 -> 565.515 seconds. These adverse movements are not accepted as noise or claimed as qualified observer-free results. The separate 4,114-file profiles captured baseline main plus four hash workers, and clone main: clone samples concentrate in native-staged-file publication, lstat, realpath, staged-directory validation and fchmod. Native thread cost is included in process CPU, though V8 profiles do not expose native worker stacks.

Functional owner probes passed: read-only retained clone bytes remain independent after a source overwrite; ctime-only hard-link churn falls back for the entire attempt and preserves the sibling native helper. The full clone count arm succeeded without fallback. These are Stage 1 proofs; broader production and platform qualification remain deferred. Cold timing remains unmeasured.


### Disposition and follow-up

The public per-file clone API repeats root/parent admission and staged publication sufficiently often to outweigh the removed digest work. Directory-relative batch admission is the next lever: one admitted directory handle, no-follow leaf opens/clones from admitted descriptors, and carried metadata. That requires a new supported `@openclaw/fs-safe` API and separate maintainer approval; no dependency change or private API is proposed here.

Historical attribution estimated 10–25% retention wall/CPU for reducing admission in the current backend; a combined cheap-admission/clone path had an optimistic 30–60% range. Both are unvalidated engineering estimates, not results from this prototype. A successor requires new counts and fresh qualified timing. Prototype production delta: +267/-35 (net +232); committed workload: +143 lines. Synthetic fixtures and lane caches are being removed; the prototype branch remains available for reference.

title: fix(plugins): voicecall and googlemeet CLIs fall back to local state when a remote Gateway is unreachable
body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/159509

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: with a remote Gateway configured (`gateway.mode: "remote"` or `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_URL`) and that Gateway unreachable, `openclaw voicecall` and `openclaw googlemeet` silently fall back to this machine's local runtime or state. `voicecall status` answers from the local call store with exit 0, and `voicecall call` / `googlemeet join` would act from this machine.

## User Impact

User impact: when the configured remote Gateway (or the tunnel to it) is down, these commands now report the unreachable Gateway and exit nonzero instead of answering for, or acting from, the wrong machine. Without a remote Gateway the existing local fallback is unchanged, and a reachable Gateway behaves as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159223 established that a CLI must never fall back to local state when a remote Gateway is unreachable; core applies it through `canFallbackToImplicitLocalGateway` and the logs fallback, and the Workboard plugin through its in-plugin `hasConfiguredRemoteGatewayTarget`. The voice-call (`callVoiceCallGateway`) and Google Meet (`callGoogleMeetGateway`) fallback predicates treated any pre-connect transport close as "run locally" without checking the target.

Both predicates now also require that no remote Gateway is configured, using the same module-private check as Workboard (`OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_URL` set, or `gateway.mode === "remote"`). When that applies, voice-call raises its existing operational error ("Gateway connection at ... failed") and Google Meet rethrows the transport error. Google Meet's fallback for a reachable Gateway that lacks the Meet methods is unchanged (the Gateway was reached).

Design note: the plugin SDK does not export the core `isImplicitLocalGatewayTarget`, so this keeps the check plugin-local, matching the existing Workboard copy, rather than adding public SDK surface in a bug fix. With three plugins now carrying the same check, a shared `openclaw/plugin-sdk/gateway-runtime` helper would be a reasonable follow-up.

## Evidence

Tested at `b6100f54b694746e3e2efada19bc280669237b5b` (base upstream/main `cd481e80875d6a1ce0092982f59e465352cd480f`).

Both sides were built from source on Linux (Node 24.18.0) by a before/after harness that runs each side in its own isolated home; every command runs through `pnpm --silent openclaw`. Each side enables voice-call with its credential-free `mock` provider, then points `gateway.remote.url` at `ws://127.0.0.1:9` (nothing listens) with `gateway.mode: "remote"` and a throwaway token, so the CLI reaches the transport. Nothing is mocked inside OpenClaw.

Before (base), remote Gateway unreachable:

```text
$ openclaw voicecall status --json
{
  "found": true,
  "calls": []
}                                   exit 0   (this machine's local call store)
```

After (this PR), same config:

```text
$ openclaw voicecall status --json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "cli_error",
    "message": "Gateway connection at ws://127.0.0.1:9 failed: Gateway not reachable at ws://127.0.0.1:9 (ECONNREFUSED). ... Source: config gateway.remote.url ... Check gateway.auth and `openclaw gateway status`, then retry."
  }
}                                   exit 1
```

Google Meet, same config with the Google Meet plugin enabled (`googlemeet status --json` reaches the fallback without Chrome or OAuth):

```text
before: {"found": true, "sessions": []}                     exit 0   (this machine's local runtime)
after:  {"ok": false, "error": {"type": "cli_error", "message": "Gateway not reachable at ws://127.0.0.1:9 (ECONNREFUSED). ... Source: config gateway.remote.url ..."}}   exit 1
```

Control for both plugins, identical on both sides: with `gateway.mode: "local"` on an unused port, `voicecall status --json` and `googlemeet status --json` still fall back locally (exit 0).

<details><summary>Focused tests and measured cost</summary>

- `extensions/voice-call/src/cli.test.ts`: new case "reports an unreachable remote Gateway instead of reading the local store" (fails on the base, 3 ms); file 8.2 s wall with `--maxWorkers=1`, 24 tests.
- `extensions/google-meet/src/cli-shared.gateway-fallback.test.ts`: new case "propagates an uncoded close when a remote Gateway is configured" (fails on the base, 2 ms); file 7.1 s wall, 7 tests.
- In CI (run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36302659486, job `checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-1`): `extensions/voice-call/src/cli.test.ts` 24 tests in 0.12 s, the Google Meet fallback test 7 tests in 0.03 s.
- `pnpm test:extension voice-call`: 691 tests pass. Google Meet: all 20 test files under `extensions/google-meet/src` (139 tests) pass through `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`.
- `pnpm check:changed` passes. The repository's `autoreview` skill (branch mode, up to P2) reported no actionable findings.

</details>



CI seconds (per-test durations reported by Vitest, summed per file from the CI job log on head `b6100f54b69`; module import and worker startup are not included):
- `extensions/google-meet/src/cli-shared.gateway-fallback.test.ts`: 7 tests, 30 ms in `checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-1` (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36302659486/job/108573532338)
- `extensions/voice-call/src/cli.test.ts`: 24 tests, 0.12 s in `checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-1` (same job)

body: Fixes #188220. ## What Problem This Solves A conversation's automation view omits a job that explicitly targets `session:global` when global session scope is enabled. The failure was reproduced through authenticated job creation, persisted readback, filtered listing, and the normal automation page. The saved jobs had no additional source or delivery binding that could hide the mismatch. ## User Impact Literal-global jobs are included in the selected agent's existing global conversation. Other agents' global conversations and explicitly qualified named targets keep separate bindings. Existing main aliases, per-sender targets, and read/management permissions retain their contracts; no configuration or migration is required. The same physical identity is used by automation badges, binding-change notifications, and archive handling. Named-session archive handling retains its locked binding recheck and existing permission checks. Main sessions, including global, remain protected from archival; restoring a named conversation still does not re-enable paused jobs. ## Why This Change Was Made The binding owner qualified literal `global` as an agent-prefixed named key even though execution uses the physical `global` row. A key alone also loses the agent needed to distinguish separate global conversations. The existing cached binding result now maps each physical key to its owning agent. title: fix(ui): keep copy feedback visible after leaving the copy button
body:
Related: #187924

## Why
When the pointer or keyboard focus leaves a chat message's copy button, its feedback fades out, so a "Copy failed" message can disappear before anyone reads it. Since #186061, each toolbar sets its own disclosure state, which overrides the older group-level reveal rule. The regression test could pass by checking before the fade finished, so [scheduled `main` CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41033746192) fails it only intermittently.

## What changed
- Replaced the group-level copy-feedback rule with a rule on the toolbar that holds the feedback (`.chat-group-footer` or `.chat-message-actions-row`), after the mobile rules. The existing toolbar `:focus-within` rule and the copy-feedback rule now share one block with the same five values. Footer-only values stay in a separate rule.
- The clipboard regression now waits for footer animations to finish before its opacity-aware visibility check.
- The new-session reload regression now waits until the stored draft includes the chosen permission. The quota case now rejects writes to the current `chatComposer.v4` key and asserts that at least one write was rejected.

## Scope
- Covers one CSS fix and three browser-test corrections. No persistence policy, schema, retention or migration change.
- Does not change mobile keyboard focus, which still reveals neighboring actions in the same group, as it does on `main`.
- Does not address the intermittent composer picker layout failure. Its cause is still unknown.

## Tradeoffs
- A wider group-level selector would also reveal footers of messages that show no feedback, so the rule targets only the owning toolbar.
- A separate feedback block added 157 B of raw CSS and failed the CSS size check, so the feedback rule shares the existing focus block. More specific mobile and peer rules still take precedence over it.
- The draft write keeps its 200 ms debounce. The reload test waits for the committed draft instead of the product flushing on every permission change.

## Blast Radius
Control UI chat toolbars only. While feedback shows, that toolbar's other actions render at the 0.6 desktop disclosed opacity, which briefly dims them on touch devices. After focus leaves, copy feedback stays on its own toolbar. Without this fix, these browser tests keep failing intermittently in `main` and PR CI, including #187924.

## Verification
- Clipboard: the updated test fails on the old CSS at 1280 px and 390 px and passes with the fix, in local Chromium with the production bundle and a mock Gateway.
- CSS size: on the base of the failed CI check, total CSS grows by 36 B raw and 12 B gzip, down from 157 B raw. That is within the unchanged 64 B allowance over a base that already exceeds the fixed caps. This is a local macOS measurement, not a passing Linux CI run.
- Draft and quota: a stored-draft read found no permission while the selector already showed read-only. The CI reload failure itself did not reproduce locally. With the old `v2` key, the quota assertion fails with 0 rejections. With the volatile retry fallback disabled, the corrected case fails. The full prompt and attachments file passed 11/11 before a lint-only parameter rename.
- The author's 20 focused and 6 consumer checks of the CSS change pass. Independent QA passed 39 cases across the affected browser suites on the first commit, the reload and quota cases on the second, and focused toolbar checks on the CSS size commit in touch-emulated mobile Chromium. A side-by-side run found focus behavior identical before and after the size change.
- Independent source reviews of each commit found no P0–P2 defect. The review panel's one actionable finding, the quota false green, is fixed here. Scoped types, lint, format and ratchet checks pass. No CI result is claimed here.

The SQLite writer metric label `sessions` is a catch-all for every `session.*` command without an exact name. ## Why This Change Was Made

The exporter series cap is unchanged; at most 30 new label values reach the worker families, within their reserves (request/queue-wait 512, phase 1,024; production uses about 180 and 700).

They weren't needed for the catch-all, they would have broken the established family queries used for current before/after comparisons (for example plugin-state request bytes), and they would have added series pressure on an exporter that already drops series.

Production LOC: **+30**, all static vocabulary entries. Explicit names are necessary to preserve bounded cardinality without importing database owners into the low-level classifier. title: fix(msteams): expire pending uploads across clock changes
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an in-memory Teams pending upload (a file waiting for FileConsentCard approval) can be dropped while still fresh, or kept past its TTL, when the system clock steps (NTP correction, manual change, VM snapshot restore). Besides the 5-minute TTL timer, `getPendingUpload` runs an explicit age check for the case where the timer has not fired yet, and that check compares `Date.now()` readings — so a backward step keeps stale uploads alive and a forward step makes the user's Accept click hit an already-gone file.

## User Impact

Pending uploads expire exactly at their 5-minute TTL regardless of system-clock corrections, and fresh uploads are never dropped early by a forward clock jump. No configuration, public API, schema, or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The explicit expiry check is an in-process duration decision, so it now rides a monotonic deadline (`performance.now()`), which is immune to system-clock steps. The public `createdAt` field keeps its epoch value for API consumers, and the TTL timer itself is unchanged.

## Evidence

`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/msteams/src/pending-uploads.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/pending-uploads.lifecycle.test.ts`: 7/7 pass. The stale-entry case now advances the monotonic clock without firing timers, and a new regression keeps fresh entries across one-hour wall-clock steps in both directions (red against the base implementation). `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` clean on changed files. Local tsgo lane unavailable on this host (glibc 2.28 vs binary requirement 2.33+); type gates run in hosted CI. Net test growth +10 lines is recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/chengzhichao-msteams-uploads-clock-20261030.txt`.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** The shipped Teams file-consent callback (`runMSTeamsFileConsentInvokeHandler`) must still find a fresh pending upload after a wall-clock step.
**Real environment tested:** This branch at HEAD `b0d8d53915f766304669bd9791d4629cf1ca3206`, Node v24.13.1, Linux x64; a real subprocess drives the shipped consent handler end to end: real in-memory store plus a real sqlite-backed plugin-state store (isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`) for the FS fallback path. `Date.now` is stepped forward one hour after a real `storePendingUpload`; `performance.now` stays native. The synthetic upload URL is rejected by the SSRF allowlist as designed, which is what marks reaching the upload stage.
**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `WT=$PWD OUT=/tmp/clock-proof/msteams-invoke-head.json node --import tsx /tmp/clock-proof/msteams-invoke.mts`, then the same command with `extensions/msteams/src/pending-uploads.ts` restored to the base revision.
**Evidence after fix:** HEAD terminal output: `{"reachedUploadStage":true,"expiredPath":false,"activities":["File upload failed. Please try again."]}` — the fresh upload is found after the step, the handler proceeds to the upload stage, and only the synthetic URL stops it. BASE under the identical step: `{"reachedUploadStage":false,"expiredPath":true,"activities":["The file upload request has expired. Please try sending the file again."]}` — the fresh upload is wrongly expired before the user is ever served. Receipts: `/tmp/clock-proof/msteams-invoke-{head,base}.json`.
**Observed result after fix:** A fresh consent accept reaches the upload stage after a one-hour forward wall-clock step; base reports the request as expired instead.
**What was not tested:** Teams live delivery, Graph upload, the fs-backed pending-upload variant (see below), and OS/NTP clock adjustment. The earlier helper-level red/green pair (driving `storePendingUpload`/`getPendingUpload` directly, `freshEntrySurvivesForwardStep` true-vs-false) remains as supplementary evidence.

## Intentionally out of scope

- `pending-uploads-fs.ts`: the fs-backed variant persists `createdAt` across restarts, so its expiry must stay on epoch time by design (a monotonic reading cannot cross a process restart).
- TTL length, timer behavior, and the consent-card flow.

title: fix(irc): reset reconnect backoff across clock changes
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: IRC reconnect delays stay stuck near the 30-second cap after a stable connection, or reset too early while a peer keeps flapping, when the system clock steps (NTP correction, manual change, VM snapshot restore). The reconnect backoff decides whether a connection stayed up for the 60-second stability window by comparing `Date.now()` readings, so a backward step erases accumulated uptime and a forward step fabricates it.

## User Impact

Reconnect delays recover to the 1-second initial delay after a stable minute even if the system clock jumps, and a forward clock jump no longer lets a repeatedly dropped connection hammer the server. No configuration, public API, schema, or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Uptime is a duration, not a wall-clock reading. The stability window now reads `performance.now()`, which is monotonic and immune to system-clock steps; backoff policy values, jitter, and the reset threshold are unchanged, and no timestamps leave the process. Existing tests now drive the monotonic clock, and two regressions pin a backward step after a stable minute and a forward step during a fresh connection.

## Evidence

`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/irc/src/reconnect-backoff.test.ts`: 5/5 pass (both new wall-clock regressions are red against the base implementation). `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` clean on changed files. Local tsgo lane unavailable on this host (glibc 2.28 vs binary requirement 2.33+); type gates run in hosted CI. Net test growth +30 lines is recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/chengzhichao-irc-backoff-clock-20261030.txt` for the two wall-clock regressions.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** IRC reconnect scheduling through the shipped `monitorIrcProvider` boundary must survive wall-clock steps in both directions.
**Real environment tested:** This branch at HEAD `5b36005a7401a32f5b70e1fe8d68b469a523122b`, Node v24.13.1, Linux x64. The real `monitorIrcProvider` runs against a real loopback TCP server with REAL timers throughout; only `Date.now` is stepped (+/-120s) between a disconnect and the next scheduled reconnect while `performance.now` stays native. The server records each connection arrival; the reported delay is measured at the socket boundary, not read from the implementation.
**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/irc/src/monitor-clock-step.proof.test.ts` (throwaway harness driving the shipped monitor; not committed), then the identical command with `extensions/irc/src/reconnect-backoff.ts` restored to the base revision.
**Evidence after fix:** Terminal output, HEAD:

```
PROOF forward: scheduled reconnect delay = 2256ms (uptime 500ms)   # attempt 2, no premature reset
PROOF backward: scheduled reconnect delay = 1141ms (uptime 60000ms) # reset after a stable minute
```

BASE (same harness, same perturbation):

```
PROOF forward: scheduled reconnect delay = 1183ms (uptime 500ms)   # prematurely reset to attempt 1
PROOF backward: scheduled reconnect delay = 2039ms (uptime 60000ms) # reset lost after a stable minute
```

Both cases flip as required (base fails the harness assertions; head passes).
**Observed result after fix:** The shipped monitor's actual reconnect timer follows monotonic connection uptime: a forward wall-clock step no longer resets a fresh connection's backoff (2256ms, attempt-2 band), and a backward step no longer erases a stable minute (1141ms, reset band). Base behavior inverts both.
**What was not tested:** Live IRC networks, TLS registration paths, OS/NTP clock adjustment, and the gateway host process. Backoff policy values themselves are unchanged. The earlier helper-level red/green pair (driving `createIrcReconnectBackoff` directly, forward step 2000-vs-1000, backward step 1000-vs-2000) remains as supplementary evidence.

## Intentionally out of scope

- Other IRC timing reads that already use the monotonic clock, and channels whose probes were fixed separately.
- Any change to reconnect policy constants or jitter.

title: fix(channels): preserve IRC timing and Teams uploads across clock changes
body:
## What Problem This Solves

IRC reconnect delays and probe latency, and fresh Teams file-consent uploads, become incorrect when the system clock changes.

Related: #188237, #188238, #188239. This combines chengzhichao-xydt's three fixes and retains their commits, including the updated IRC probe consumer fix.

## User Impact

IRC reconnects retain their normal backoff and healthy-connection reset policy, probes report elapsed connection time, and Teams users can accept a fresh file upload despite a wall-clock correction. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use `performance.now()` directly for these process-local durations. Teams keeps its public `createdAt` epoch unchanged and adds a private monotonic expiry deadline; filesystem-backed, cross-process upload expiry remains unchanged. No SDK API is added.

Consolidated the regressions into the existing owner/consumer suites, removed the duplicate probe suite and test allocations, and made the IRC monitor's fake clock include performance. Against the merge base: production **+14 lines**, tests **0 net lines**. The private Teams deadline is needed to preserve the public epoch field without measuring expiry against it.

## Evidence

Built main `ac32225fbbbc799eaa43dd1666e81a25bdb54b9d` and candidate `d3a4f387b5e0c1314ad270fd6773fd38045eaab6` in secretless Docker on Node 24.22.1. Used the built Gateway, explicit isolated profiles and state/config/database paths. Only `Date.now()` was stepped inside the process; native timers, `performance.now()`, reconnect jitter and the real 60-second stable window were unchanged.

Final head `e7fdbe41f93dbc53f5f1aa0028634e213d8c0439` only repairs test cleanup typing and uses complete fake timers in two suites; all production files are identical to the built candidate above, so the runtime evidence is reused unchanged. The three adjusted suites were rerun: **45/45 tests passed**. This fixes the initial head's `check-test-types` cleanup callback error and `check-lint` formatting failures rather than rerunning those jobs.

[Sanitized runtime capture and before/after results](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188293#issuecomment-6521663467).

Two iterations on each revision:

| Real Gateway path | Main | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| IRC `channels.status` probe, local TCP registration delayed ~300 ms, ±1-hour wall steps | −3,599,662 / −3,599,573 ms; +3,600,315 / +3,600,355 ms | All stepped probes 310–447 ms |
| IRC monitor, forward step after a short connection | Incorrectly reset to 1,065 / 1,070 ms | Preserved growing backoff: 4,551 / 4,637 ms |
| IRC monitor, backward step after 61 real seconds connected | Incorrectly retained 4,786 / 4,766 ms | Reset normally: 1,154 / 1,194 ms |
| Teams inbound agent reply → real messenger FileConsentCard → authenticated accept invoke, +360,001 ms step | Same-process memory lookup lost fresh entry; no upload, expired response | Same-process entry found; actual 51-byte upload and replacement FileInfoCard on both accepts |

Controls passed on both revisions: unstepped IRC probes, increasing short-connection backoff, ordinary reset after 61 seconds; Teams ordinary accepted upload, conversation mismatch rejection followed by a valid accept, decline cleanup, and natural expiry after a real five-minute wait. Invalid-signature and wrong-audience Teams webhooks returned HTTP 401. Candidate recorded six exact-byte upload PUTs with `Content-Range: bytes 0-50/51` and six corresponding original-card updates across the stepped accepts and ordinary controls.

Teams proof used the normal App/Express authentication and sender/URL guards with synthetic RSA/JWKS identity infrastructure and a loopback Connector/upload transport. Production Connector authority interceptors and middleware remained installed. Temporary observation hooks in both builds recorded the actual messenger store and consent getter with the same Gateway PID; no direct helper invocation, auth bypass or CLI filesystem-backed send was used. A deterministic local Responses provider generated the attachment replies.

Focused checks: **41/41 tests passed** across reconnect-backoff, send/probe and pending-upload suites; **19/19 passed** across IRC monitor, Teams consent handler and pending-upload lifecycle consumers. The same current owner regressions against main produced **6 failures / 35 passes**, covering all three clock defects. Changed-file formatting and lint passed.

Merge danger: **two-way door**; reverting restores the former duration calculations without changing persisted data or configuration. Blast radius is IRC reconnect/probe timing and same-process Teams pending uploads; filesystem-backed Teams uploads and other channels are untouched.

Closes #181686

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes offline `models status --probe` reporting `unknown` for account-owned SecretRefs even when the referenced credential is available.

## User Impact

Operators can check environment- and protected-store-backed account credentials offline, while unresolved references remain unsent and resolved credentials stay out of persisted profiles.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing local account-secret preparation owner before inference, inside the probe's exclusive offline state ownership. Gateway RPC probes continue using their existing runtime snapshots. The production change adds five lines; the regression adds 137 lines to exercise the real credential and HTTP paths.

## Evidence

**Shipped CLI proof (requested in review):** [successful run](https://github.com/Maximora-byte/openclaw/actions/runs/39983882929/job/120517911766) builds exact PR head `9dfef9601418cf0d93d4eab28d4ffd2db0a2f830` with `pnpm build:runtime` on Node 24.22.1 and pnpm 12.15.0, then launches the shipped `node openclaw.mjs models status --probe` entry point in four isolated temporary state roots.

It counts real HTTP requests and verifies their authorization at an isolated local endpoint. After each subprocess exits, it reads the canonical shared SQLite profile store read-only to compare the saved credentials before and after probing. title: fix(codex): unblock session deletion after an older generation retires
body:
Related: #144179
Previous candidate: #144396 (closed without merging)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: deleting a session fails with a generation-change error when its Codex binding is already cleared and retired but belongs to an older physical session generation.

## User Impact

Users can delete these sessions and prune expired synthetic sessions without an inert predecessor binding blocking the operation. This addresses the retired-binding variant of #144179; active predecessor bindings and cleared bindings without the retired marker remain protected.

## Why This Change Was Made

The deletion-specific eligibility check now accepts an explicitly cleared, retired predecessor through the existing binding lifecycle. The ordinary generation ownership check and the worker's authority, lease, conditional removal and compensation checks remain unchanged. The assertion belongs beside the existing generation-aware record rules, keeping the binding orchestrator within its current line cap.

Thanks to @datenpapst for the report and @0xalydev for the original candidate in #144396. That PR closed unmerged after its requested real SQLite and product-path proof remained outstanding; its closing discussion allows a fresh proof-backed repair. This change supplies that proof and preserves the non-retired refusal and exact rollback contracts. AI-assisted implementation and validation; independently reviewed before submission.

Base: `1e906e96143645c19df9f313638d5b4edb44c011`. Final candidate: `9d869a859a57c581e2707bc8741ee6165182a11a`. Before submission, current main `200afde2c1866d3f5ec047e65716b3d96df0648d` still matched the base for these three TypeScript files.

- **Red:** the new retired-predecessor case failed on the base through the real SQLite/native worker with `Codex binding generation changed before session deletion`. A separately built base Gateway reproduced the same error through normal `sessions.delete`, retaining the session and companion.
- **Final candidate:** 54 owner tests passed, including all 16 real SQLite deletion/settlement cases and 38 Codex binding cases.
